title: How to join a Zoom meeting on Mac: step by step for Zoom Workplace
metaTitle: How to Join a Zoom Meeting on Mac: Step by Step
description: How to join a Zoom meeting on Mac from an invite link or Zoom Workplace, with menu paths, shortcuts and fixes for common join problems.
targetKeyword: how to join a zoom meeting on mac
secondaryKeywords: join zoom meeting with meeting ID mac
intro: To join a Zoom meeting on Mac, click the invite link and choose to open it in Zoom Workplace. With no link, open Zoom Workplace, choose Join a meeting, and enter the meeting ID and passcode.
tldr: Click the invite link and choose to open it in Zoom Workplace, or open Zoom Workplace and click Join a meeting.
Enter the meeting ID and passcode if you have no link. You do not need a Zoom account for this.
Participants click Join on the meeting card. Hosts click Start.
Check the camera and microphone on the join screen, then click Join.
If the join fails, check camera and microphone permissions under Apple menu > System Settings > Privacy & Security.

blocks.text: Install Zoom Workplace on your Mac first

Zoom's desktop app now goes by Zoom Workplace. Older guides still call it Zoom or the Zoom app, but it is the same program. Zoom renamed it to line up with the rest of its product line, according to Zoom's release notes as reported by SMU IT Connect.

If you do not have the app yet, open zoom.us/download in your browser. Under Zoom Workplace for Mac, click Download for Apple Silicon or Download for Intel. Pick the button that matches your Mac's processor. Apple silicon Macs are the newer models, so check your Mac's About This Mac window if you are unsure.

Then run the zoomusInstallerFull.pkg file and follow the installer. Keep the Mac connected to the internet while it runs. Do not close the installer early, or you may need to start the download again.
Your Mac needs macOS 10.15 or later for the current desktop app. Zoom's system requirements also list a dual-core processor at 2 GHz or higher and 4 GB of RAM. Zoom recommends a 64-bit system.

items: macOS 10.15 or later for the current desktop app
Dual-core 2 GHz processor or higher, with 4 GB of RAM
Version 7.0.0 dropped support for macOS 10.13 and 10.14
Version 6.7.7 was the last release built for macOS below 10.15

blocks.text: Check your macOS version before you download. Click the Apple menu, then About This Mac. The macOS version appears near the top of the window. If it is older than the minimum, install the release that matches your system instead.

You can check the Zoom version inside the app. From version 6.7.0 on, a gear Settings icon sits in the navigation bar. Older builds put settings in a different place, so the paths in this guide may differ on them.
Join from an invite link
The invite link is the fastest path. It works from an email or a calendar event. Open the message, then click the join link under Join Zoom Meeting.
Your Mac then asks which app should open the link. Choose Zoom Workplace. Zoom opens the join screen inside the app. Check your audio and video, then click Join.
If the host turned on a waiting room, you wait until the host lets you in. Keep the Zoom window open and in front while you wait. You do not need to do anything else on your side.
Some links open in your browser first. If the page does nothing, go back to the invite and choose the app option again. The app has to be installed for that option to appear.
Calendar apps sometimes show the link inside a small card. Click the link text itself. Clicking the card around it may only open the event details.
Join with a meeting ID and passcode

Use this path when someone gives you numbers instead of a link. The meeting ID identifies the meeting. The passcode is a separate code that lets you in. Ask the host for both before the meeting starts.

Open Zoom Workplace. If you are not signed in, the first screen offers Sign in, Join a meeting, or Sign up. You do not need an account to join. Choose Join a meeting, then type the meeting ID and passcode.
Enter your name when the app asks for it. Use a name the host will recognize. Then click Join. The audio and video check comes next, on the join screen, before you enter the room.
Most failed joins on this path come from typing mistakes. Copy the meeting ID and passcode from the invite instead of retyping them from memory. Then paste them into the app.
Join from the Home, Meetings, or Calendar tab

If you have a Zoom account and the meeting is on your calendar, you can skip the link. Sign in to Zoom Workplace and click the Home, Meetings, or Calendar tab. Home lists today's meetings, so it is usually the quickest place to check.
Click the meeting, then read the button on the meeting card. Participants click Join. Hosts click Start. Those two labels make the difference between joining a call and opening one.
The left navigation normally shows Chat, Calendar, Phone, Contacts, and Hub. If a tab you need is missing, click the More tab to find the rest of the list.

blocks.title: Join or Start?
blocks.text: Join is for participants. Start is for hosts. Read the label before you click, because the two buttons do different jobs.
Check audio and video before you click Join

The join screen is your last check before anyone sees or hears you. Look at which camera and microphone Zoom picked. If you use an external webcam or headset, make sure it appears in the list. A wrong default is easy to miss.

The Settings gear holds the defaults. In the Video tab, you choose the camera and can uncheck Stop my video when joining a meeting. In the Audio tab, you choose the microphone and speakers, then click Test to check them.

Georgetown University's Mac guide describes the audio step this way. After you enter the meeting ID and your name, click Join With Computer Audio to connect your speakers and microphone. That guide comes from a university IT team, so some screen labels may differ from the current app.
Allow the camera and microphone in macOS

If Zoom shows a black box or no sound, macOS may be blocking the app. Open Apple menu > System Settings > Privacy & Security. Choose Camera, make sure Zoom is enabled, then turn it off and on again. Do the same for Microphone.

Restart after you change a permission. Then reopen Zoom Workplace and join again. If the problem stays, the troubleshooting list below covers the next checks, and the camera guide linked at the end goes deeper.
Join from your browser without the app
You can join without installing the app, but the experience is more limited. Start with the join link. Chrome and Firefox both show a prompt that asks permission before they open Zoom.

In Chrome, the first time you join from join.zoom.us, a pop-up offers Open zoom.us. Tick Always open these types of links in the associated app to skip it later. In Firefox, click Open Link. Tick Remember my choice for zoommtg links to stop the prompt.

If the host turned on Join from your browser, click Allow for the microphone and camera. Then enter your name and click Join. The Zoom Web App at app.zoom.us/wc lets you join from its Meetings tab, but it has fewer features.

blocks.text: Pick the path that fits the meeting. For a regular call, the app gives you the full set of meeting controls. The browser works when you only need to listen in or when you cannot install software on the Mac.
Keyboard shortcuts once you are in the meeting

Zoom publishes a list of default Mac shortcuts. Command plus Shift plus A mutes or unmutes your audio. Command plus Shift plus V starts or stops video. Command plus Shift plus S starts or stops screen share. You can use all three as soon as the meeting opens.
Hold the Space bar to unmute for as long as you hold it. This works well when you join muted and want to answer one question. Let go to mute again.
Zoom's list does not include a join-audio shortcut. The closest entry is Command plus J, which joins a meeting. Treat it as a near match, not a guaranteed join-audio command.

You can change shortcuts in the desktop app's Keyboard shortcuts settings. Some shortcuts can be made global, so they work while Zoom is not in front. If a shortcut from the list does nothing, check that setting first, then update the app.
Host-only shortcuts exist too. Command plus Control plus M mutes everyone except the host. Command plus Control plus U unmutes them. Only the host can use these two.
Common mistakes when joining a Zoom meeting on Mac

items: Expecting a browser link to open the app. Choose the app option when the prompt appears.
Looking for an old Zoom menu path. Settings moved to a gear icon from version 6.7.0 on.
Joining from the web app and expecting every feature. The Zoom Web App has limited features.
Blaming Zoom for a black camera when macOS blocks it. Check Privacy & Security first.
Clicking Start when you are a participant. Participants click Join, and hosts click Start.
Hunting for the passcode after you open the app. Get the meeting ID and passcode before you start.

blocks.text: Most of these mistakes are easy to avoid before the meeting starts. Open Zoom Workplace early, read the meeting card, and run the audio and video check once.
A worked example: joining a client call from an invite
Say a client sends a calendar invite for a call later today. You use a MacBook, and Zoom Workplace is not installed yet. Start with the invite email, not the browser.

Click the join link under Join Zoom Meeting. Your Mac may send the link to a browser first. If the page offers the app, choose Zoom Workplace. If the app is missing, download it from zoom.us/download, then click the link again.

On the join screen, check that the right microphone and camera are selected. Click Join. If the client's meeting has a waiting room, you see a waiting message until the client admits you. That is normal, so keep the window open.
If the client sent a meeting ID instead of a link, the path changes only at the start. You type the ID and passcode instead of clicking a link. Everything after the join screen stays the same.
Edge cases: work Macs, managed installs and phones
A work Mac may block installs or hide the Zoom app. Your IT team usually sets those rules, not you. Ask them whether Zoom Workplace is approved before you try to download it.
If you only have a phone, the steps change. The iPhone and Android apps have their own join screens. This guide covers the Mac only, so check Zoom's mobile help pages for those devices.
If a link keeps failing, ask the host to send it again before you spend time on fixes. A fresh invite costs less time than troubleshooting a link that never worked.
When the join fails: fixes that work
The fixes below cover the causes that Zoom's support pages and third-party guides describe. Start with the one that matches what you see on screen.
Update the app first. Look in the Zoom menu in the menu bar for Check for Updates. Menu wording changes between versions, so search the menus if you do not see it.
Quit other apps that use the camera, such as FaceTime or Messenger. Then rejoin. MacPaw's guide recommends this step for camera problems on a Mac.
Check that the camera and microphone you want are selected in Settings. Then confirm that macOS allows Zoom to use both. Restart after any permission change.

If you see a message about the meeting not starting, this guide could not confirm Zoom's exact wording for it. Wait a little, check the start time on the invite, and ask the host to start the meeting.
Why setup takes longer than you expect
Joining is more than one click for many people. Owl Labs surveyed 2,000 US full-time workers in July 2025. The report found that 67% had tried to set up video tech for a meeting and given up.

On average, employees lose over six minutes getting hybrid meetings started, according to the same survey. These numbers describe video technology in general, not Zoom alone. Owl Labs sells meeting hardware, so read them as a sign that join trouble is common.
The practical lesson is to set up early. Open Zoom Workplace before the start time, run the audio and video check, then wait. You lose less time when the setup is already done.
Where to go next

Once you are in, the next task is usually sharing your screen. [Share your screen in Zoom on Mac](/how-to/share-your-screen-in-zoom) covers the desktop steps and black screen fixes. If the camera still will not start, [grant camera access in Zoom on Mac](/how-to/grant-camera-access-in-zoom) walks through System Settings in more detail.

If you want a background behind you, [change your virtual background in Zoom on Mac](/how-to/change-your-virtual-background-in-zoom) shows where that setting lives. To keep a copy of the call, see [how to record a Zoom meeting on Mac](/how-to/record-a-meeting-in-zoom).

faq.question: Do I need a Zoom account to join a meeting on my Mac?
faq.answer: No. On first launch, Zoom Workplace offers Join a meeting. Choose it, then enter the meeting ID and passcode. An account helps if you want the Home, Meetings, and Calendar tabs that list your scheduled meetings.

faq.question: Why does Chrome ask me to Open zoom.us when I join?
faq.answer: The join.zoom.us link hands the meeting to the Zoom app on your Mac. The first time, Chrome shows a pop-up. Tick Always open these types of links in the associated app to skip the pop-up later.

faq.question: What is the difference between Join and Start?
faq.answer: Join is the button for participants. Start is the button for hosts. Both appear on the meeting card in Zoom Workplace, so read the label before you click.

faq.question: Is the browser version of Zoom as good as the app?
faq.answer: Not quite. The Zoom Web App at app.zoom.us/wc lets you join from the Meetings tab, but it has limited features. Use Zoom Workplace when you need the full set of meeting controls.

faq.question: What macOS version do I need for Zoom Workplace?
faq.answer: Zoom's current minimum for the desktop app is macOS 10.15 or later. Version 7.0.0 dropped macOS 10.13 and 10.14. Version 6.7.7 was the last release for macOS below 10.15.

faq.question: I joined, but nobody can hear me. What do I check?
faq.answer: Open the gear Settings icon and check the Audio tab for the right microphone and speakers. Click Test. Then confirm Zoom is allowed under Apple menu > System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone.

task: Join a Zoom meeting on a Mac
appliesTo: Zoom Workplace for macOS 10.15 or later
requirements: A Mac running macOS 10.15 or later
Zoom Workplace installed, or a browser to join from
The invite link, or the meeting ID and passcode from the host
A working microphone and camera if you plan to speak or appear on video

steps.name: Install or update Zoom Workplace
steps.text: Go to zoom.us/download and click Download for Apple Silicon or Download for Intel under Zoom Workplace for Mac. Run the zoomusInstallerFull.pkg file and follow the installer.
steps.tip: If the app is already installed, open it and check for updates before you join anything.

steps.name: Open the invite link
steps.text: From the invite email or calendar event, click the join link under Join Zoom Meeting. Choose to launch the meeting in the Zoom Workplace app. If you have no link, go to the next step.
steps.tip: If the link opens a browser page instead, go back and choose the app option.

steps.name: Choose Join a meeting or sign in
steps.text: On first launch, the app offers Sign in, Join a meeting, or Sign up. Without an account, choose Join a meeting. Signed-in users open the Home, Meetings, or Calendar tab and click the meeting.

steps.name: Enter the meeting ID and passcode
steps.text: Type the meeting ID and passcode the host sent. Enter your name when the app asks for it. Then click Join.
steps.tip: Ask the host for both codes before the meeting starts, not during it.

steps.name: Check audio and video on the join screen
steps.text: Confirm the camera and microphone Zoom selected are the ones you want. If you see Join With Computer Audio, click it to connect your speakers and microphone.
steps.tip: The Video tab holds your camera choice. You can also uncheck Stop my video when joining a meeting there.

steps.name: Allow camera and microphone in macOS
steps.text: If Zoom shows no picture or no sound, open Apple menu > System Settings > Privacy & Security. Choose Camera, confirm Zoom is enabled, then turn it off and on. Repeat the steps for Microphone.
steps.tip: Restart after you change a permission, then reopen Zoom Workplace and join again.

steps.name: Click Join and wait if needed
steps.text: Click Join. If the host has a waiting room on, you wait there until the host admits you. The meeting opens for you once you are let in.
steps.tip: Keep the Zoom window open and in front while you wait, so you do not miss the admit.

steps.name: Find the in-meeting toolbar
steps.text: The toolbar at the bottom holds Audio, Video, Participants, Chat, Share, and More. If it hides, move the mouse inside the window. Press Command plus Shift plus A to mute and Command plus Shift plus V to stop video.
steps.tip: Hold the Space bar to unmute briefly, then let go to mute again.

troubleshooting.problem: The join link does nothing when I click it
troubleshooting.fix: Install Zoom Workplace from zoom.us/download, then click the link again and choose the app option. In Chrome, answer the Open zoom.us prompt. If nothing still happens, ask the host to resend the invite.

troubleshooting.problem: No picture, or a black video box
troubleshooting.fix: Open Apple menu > System Settings > Privacy & Security > Camera, confirm Zoom is on, turn it off and on, then restart. Quit FaceTime or Messenger if they hold the camera, and check the camera in Settings.

troubleshooting.problem: Nobody can hear me, or I cannot hear anyone
troubleshooting.fix: Open the gear Settings icon and check the Audio tab for the right microphone and speakers. Click Test. Then confirm Zoom is allowed under Apple menu > System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone.

troubleshooting.problem: A message says the meeting has not started
troubleshooting.fix: This guide could not verify Zoom's exact wording for that message. Wait a little, check the start time on the invite, and ask the host to start the meeting.

troubleshooting.problem: Zoom will not open on my Mac
troubleshooting.fix: Check that your Mac runs macOS 10.15 or later, the current minimum. On an older Mac, use 6.7.7, the last release built for macOS below 10.15.
